gaps.sentence: Try to be ___ when you cross the busy road (CARE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'be': careful (-ful). 'Carefully' is an adverb and cannot follow 'be'.
The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unusual. An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: The hospital provides ___ care around the clock (PERSON).
gaps.hint: adjective needed before the noun 'care'; beware the word meaning 'staff'
gaps.explanation: 'Personal care' uses the adjective 'personal'; 'personnel' is a noun meaning staff.

gaps.sentence: Her answer was ___ , so we had to ask again (RELEVANT).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — it did not relate to the question
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'relevant' is 'irrelevant' (ir- before r). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: We must ___ our efforts to finish on time (STRONG).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: strengthen. A base verb follows 'must'.

gaps.sentence: Being blamed for something you didn't do is completely ___ (FAIR).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed after 'is', and the situation is negative: unfair (un- + fair).

gaps.sentence: He is one of the best ___ (SCIENCE) in the field.
gaps.hint: plural person needed after 'one of the best'
gaps.explanation: 'One of the best' is followed by a plural noun for people: scientists.
